issues.legal_issue: A building tax imposed solely on floor area, without rationally classifying materially dissimilar buildings, violates the constitutional guarantee of equality.
material_facts: The tax applied to buildings meeting a minimum floor-area threshold and used floor area as its sole basis for determining liability and the amount of tax.
The same basis applied to buildings that differed in class, construction, use, location, capacity for profitable use, cost, and economic rental.
The legislation made no rational classification based on those or other relevant circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The charging provision violated the equality clause of the Constitution, and the appeals challenging the High Court’s decision were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A taxing law must be within legislative competence and consistent with the Constitution; its validity may be challenged for violating fundamental rights. Under Articles 13(2), 14 and 265, a tax imposed by law cannot deny equality. Fiscal legislation allows the legislature broad discretion in classification, but imposing a uniform tax on essentially dissimilar persons, objects or transactions may deny equality when the legislature fails to make a rational classification. The Court relied on K.T. Moopil Nair v. State of Kerala, Khandige Sham Bhat v. Agricultural Income-tax Officer, Shri Ram Krishna Dalmia v. Shri Justice S.R. Tendolkar, and applied New Manek Chowk Spinning and Weaving Mills Co. Ltd. v. Municipal Corporation of the City of Ahmedabad. The Court left open whether taxing only buildings completed after the legislation took effect, while exempting earlier buildings, violated equality.

rule.if: constitutional_tax_challenge and tax_based_only_on_floor_area and covers_materially_different_buildings and omits_relevant_taxation_characteristics

predicates.constitutional_tax_challenge: A person challenges the validity of a taxing law on constitutional equality grounds.
predicates.tax_based_only_on_floor_area: The legislature bases liability and the amount of a building tax solely on the building’s floor area.
predicates.covers_materially_different_buildings: The tax applies on the same basis to buildings that differ in relevant characteristics such as class, construction, use, location, or capacity for profitable use.
predicates.omits_relevant_taxation_characteristics: The legislature does not take relevant differences between buildings into account when classifying them for taxation.

issues.definition: When a constitutional tax challenge concerns a tax based only on floor area that covers materially different buildings and omits relevant taxation characteristics, the charging rule denies equal protection.
